title: Add prints the bare id
lead: `slicer add TITLE --print-id` writes only the item's id and a newline to stdout, so a script can capture it with `id=$(slicer add "…" --print-id)` without `--json` and a JSON parser.
findings_note: owner request, 2026-10-15: file an item and get back only its id; today add prints a human line or JSON
boundary: **Not in this slice:** a `--print-id` on `import` (it files several ids; `import --json` gives `ids`); a separate `new` command (the owner's question was answered by `add`); changing the default text line.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: On 2026-10-15 the owner asked for a command that files a new item and returns its id. `add` already allocates the next free id and reports it, but only inside a line meant for people (`added S01  Probe one`, `cmd_add`, `src/slicer/cli.py:2070`) or inside the JSON payload. A shell script has to parse one or the other: piping `--json` output through jq needs jq, and cutting the text line depends on wording that is free to change. `--render` adds a second stdout line (`rendered 2 file(s)`), so even taking the first line is fragile. `next-id` prints a bare id but does not allocate, so using it before `add --id` races with other filings.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py`:
  - `add` gets `--print-id`: stdout is exactly `<id>\n`, for a new item and for a `--key` retry that returns an existing one alike.
  - Under `--print-id`, the render summary that `--render` prints goes to stderr instead of stdout. The stderr hints (unscored, undeclared pass) are unchanged, and so are exit codes and errors.
  - `--print-id` with `--json` is `usage` (exit 2), and nothing is written.
- `docs/commands.md` (the `add` row), `docs/agents.md` (the `add` row: `--print-id` is the text form; the JSON payload is unchanged), `CHANGELOG.md` under Added.
- `tests/test_add_options.py`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Add_PrintId_StdoutIsBareId`: `add T --print-id` writes exactly `<id>\n` to stdout and files the item.
- `test_Add_PrintIdWithKeyRetry_PrintsExistingId`: a second `add T --key K --print-id` prints the first item's id and files nothing new.
- `test_Add_PrintIdWithRender_RenderLineOnStderr`: with `--render`, stdout is still only the id.
- `test_Add_PrintIdWithJson_Usage`: exit 2, `usage`, index bytes unchanged.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red.
2. Add the flag in the `add` parser and branch on it in `cmd_add` before `_emit`; route the render summary to stderr under the flag.
3. Docs and CHANGELOG; mutation-check (print the text line instead; drop the render redirect; drop the `--json` refusal).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3.12 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` passes.
- `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
